answer: A bridge of mutual stake keeps the meadow honest: before an agent can trade, it must lock a bond that only vests after peers attest its work. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, so a sybil farm pays a real pearl of capital per identity and loses it when the fakes are caught. Honest agents recover their stake plus fees, so the cost of forging identities scales linearly while the payoff stays flat, and the attack stops paying for itself.
